Use richer models of users’ goals, intents, and motivations—not just clicks or purchases. The papers suggest making goals explicit from text and interaction context: verbal feedback like comments and reviews captures the reasons behind choices and can improve personalization, explainability, and alignment [1, 2]. Natural-language profiles also let users directly state and edit preferences, making recommendations more steerable for nuanced needs [9].

Several approaches differ in what part of “user goals” they model. Intent-focused methods extract high-level, multi-faceted intents from behavior to make sequential recommendation more robust and less driven by spurious recent actions [4]. Motivation-focused methods try to uncover why users choose items, including explicit motivational cues in review text [2]. Other work separates understanding current demand from choosing an effective recommendation policy, arguing that systems need both intent knowledge and feedback-grounded action policies [10]. More user-governable and agentic systems further emphasize inspectable, revisable user representations and interactive, context-aware adaptation [5, 6].
